subject: Physics
axis_note: ladder_position is a curriculum coordinate. It is never a learner estimate; teaching depth is intrinsic, while practice percentages only route support.

must_contain: A system boundary with heat and work arrows crossing it while internal energy is labelled inside.
Two states with the same temperature but different amounts of substance to separate temperature from total internal energy.

controlled_variation.vary: direction of energy transfer across the boundary
controlled_variation.hold: the same system and initial/final states
controlled_variation.notice: heat or work can change sign as transfer direction reverses, while internal energy is a state quantity

rungs.aha: The first law is an energy balance whose signs depend on a declared work convention; with work done by the system positive, delta U = Q - W must be used consistently.
learner_owns: Internal energy is stored in the system while heat and work are boundary transfers.
Can use signed quantities in an energy balance.
must_contain: A boundary diagram paired with one explicit sign convention before any equation is used.
Compression and expansion cases using the same convention.

misconception.wrong_idea: Work is always a positive energy loss, so its sign never needs to be tracked.
misconception.diagnostic_prompt: Under the convention 'work done by the system is positive', what sign does W have during compression?
misconception.repair: State the convention first, then assign work sign from boundary motion; do not mix 'by-system' and 'on-system' formulas.

rungs.closure: For two heating/compression scenarios, assign signs to Q and W under one declared convention and predict the sign of delta U before calculating magnitudes.

controlled_variation.hold: the same sign convention and heat input
controlled_variation.notice: the work term changes sign while the convention itself does not

controlled_variation.vary: choice of convention from work-by-system to work-on-system
controlled_variation.notice: the algebraic form changes but the predicted physical delta U does not

must_contain: Two distinct paths between the same endpoints on a Cartesian P-V plot.
Different areas under the two paths paired with the same endpoint delta U.

controlled_variation.hold: initial state, final state, and sign convention
controlled_variation.notice: work changes with path while delta U stays fixed

controlled_variation.vary: path shape on the P-V plot
controlled_variation.notice: the area under the path changes even though the state-function change does not

must_contain: A closed clockwise P-V loop with the enclosed area highlighted and each leg direction marked.
The same loop traversed in the opposite direction to expose the sign of net work.

controlled_variation.notice: the sign of net work reverses while the magnitude of the enclosed area is unchanged

controlled_variation.hold: the same qualitative cycle shape and direction
controlled_variation.notice: larger enclosed area means larger magnitude of net work per cycle

must_contain: An energy-flow diagram with Q_in from the hot reservoir, W_out, and Q_out to the cold reservoir.
Two engines between the same reservoir temperatures, one claimed above the reversible temperature bound.

controlled_variation.notice: the maximum efficiency changes with the reservoir-temperature ratio
a real-engine efficiency may fall below the bound but cannot exceed it

family.invariant_demand: Declare the system and sign convention, distinguish state quantities from transfers, choose a valid process or cycle relation, use the P-V representation when needed, and check energy balance plus second-law bounds.
family.difficult_move: Deciding what belongs to the state and what belongs to the path, while keeping one sign convention consistent through the entire process.
family.independent_check: Close the energy ledger and test a boundary case: a cycle must give delta U=0, reversed path work must change sign, and an engine efficiency must not exceed its reservoir-temperature bound.

support_ladder.handed_over: The system boundary, sign convention, and process type are stated; the learner completes the energy ledger and validity check.
The system boundary and initial/final states are marked, but the learner chooses the sign convention and process relation.
Only the process description, state data, and requested quantity are given.

transfer.changed_demand: A rapid expansion is described as insulated but not quasi-static; decide which ideal-process relations are justified beyond Q=0.
transfer.information_not_handed_over: whether reversibility or a quasi-static path may be assumed from the word 'adiabatic' alone

transfer.changed_demand: A P-V loop is supplied without a process table; infer net work sign and magnitude relation from its direction and enclosed area.
transfer.information_not_handed_over: the mapping from loop orientation and area to signed net work

transfer.changed_demand: Two different paths connect the same endpoints and one path's work is known; determine the other path's heat using endpoint data.
transfer.information_not_handed_over: that delta U is shared by both paths while work differs

transfer.changed_demand: A refrigerator is presented instead of a heat engine; identify why a simple engine-efficiency ratio is no longer the requested performance measure.
transfer.information_not_handed_over: which energy transfer is the useful output in the reversed-cycle device
